findings.what: The screen says dt 'moves to the right' and calls this shorthand for integrating both sides over time, but never shows what gets integrated. The brief promised to show this once. Add the honest line (1 ÷ v) dv/dt = −1 ÷ RC and 'integrate both sides over t' before the shorthand dv ÷ v = −dt ÷ RC. The screen is 65 words, so there is room.

0.368 is only stated as what the window reads. Nothing on screen ties it to the solution just found. A steps lesson shows only the frame, so the explain text's e^(−1) line never reaches him. Add one short line such as 'Put t = RC into 12 e^(−t/RC): 12 e^(−1), and e^(−1) is 0.368.' Trim elsewhere to stay near 90 words.

findings.where: Screen 12, 'A coil lets go', hint after the wrong pick '0 A'
findings.what: The hint says 'The curve is still well above it', but in that state no curve is drawn. Only the red starting-rate line and the ring show. Either reword it, for example 'The fall slows as the current shrinks, so some is still left at 0.05 s', or draw the real curve faintly.

There are six footnote markers ([^1] to [^5], with [^2] used twice). Two of them, [^1] on 'their rate depends on their decay constant' and [^3] on 'gather every v on one side', mark sentences he would never look up. Drop those two and keep [^2], [^4] and [^5], which mark 0.632, 0.368 and τ = L ÷ R.

'That gives v = A e^(−t/RC), where A is e^(c)' skips the index-law step e^(−t/RC + c) = e^(c) × e^(−t/RC). It is one short sentence and he knows the law, but the screen should show it. The screen is at 84 words, so cut a word or two elsewhere.
The text stops at 'Here k is −1 ÷ 2' without the last link. Add 'So the slope is −v ÷ 2 at every t, which is the rule.'

The rate arrows are drawn in the same ink as the curve and lie along it, so only their arrowheads show. That half the voltage gives half the rate comes across through the working lines, not the picture. Draw the arrows longer or slightly offset, so the shallower arrow at 6 V reads at a glance.

Screen 3's motion ends with the window at exactly 3 s showing 2.68 V, 1.62 V and 0.607, and its text says the same. So this puzzle only asks him to recall it. Put the window somewhere he has not seen, such as 6 s, or ask the question as a prediction before screen 3.
'Try −3 ÷ 2' hands over the answer. Stop at 'Divide by RC, do not multiply.'

Screen 13's answer depends on 'each τ multiplies by e', but the screens never show this. They never write the growth curve as A e^(+t/τ), and they never name 1.649 as e^(1/2). A short phrase on screen 3, such as '1.649 is e^(1/2)', would make screen 13 a step rather than a leap.

findings.where: Lesson as a whole, compared with the brief
findings.what: The brief's plus-sign example, reactor period (the time for reactor power to change by a factor of e), is missing. It is the best growth example for a submariner heading to nuclear propulsion, so add one sentence to screen 13's Why? or to screen 3. The promised 'not every equation separates' is also missing. One sentence on screen 5 or 7 would set up lesson 4.
'Write τ for the time constant RC' uses the key term three screens before screen 11 highlights it in amber. Either give the amber highlight here or word it as 'call RC the time constant, τ'.

The 'start' label sits on the same line as the axis title, so it reads 'v (V) start'. The curve also crosses 'RC' in 'zero at one RC'. Both stay legible thanks to the halo, but the spot is crowded, so move each label a little.

findings.where: Screen 3 plot at 360 px (window at 3 s)
findings.what: The 'end' label sits on the curve, with the end rate arrow showing just under it. Nudge it up or right, clear of the curve.
The 'rule's rate' icon always points down and right. Under growth and on screen 13 the arrows rise. On screen 2 the key lists a rate arrow before Check, but none is drawn yet.

Mid-slide, dt passes over '=' and v touches '='. For a few frames the fading '/' also overlays the arriving '÷' and looks like a struck-out sign. It settles cleanly, but the paths could be spaced further apart.

The lead says 'A 12 V capacitor discharging…' and the caption says '…the rule written above the plot' on every screen. That includes the two separation screens, which have no plot, and the coil, y = 5 e^(−2t) and growth screens, which are not the capacitor. Make both general, or drop them.
'N is the number left. λ is the decay constant.' is drawn straight under a task that has just said the same thing. Drop the drawn copy.
'A discharge has one voltage. Its curve keeps one shape.' is vague. Say 'A discharge has one rate, so its curve keeps one shape.'
